title: world protocol — authoring profile
description: How to read a document you are writing yourself. Everything the wire profile asserts, plus the two things a consumer must not assert about someone else's document but an author wants asserted about their own: on a component the core vocabulary defines, a field it does not define is a typo until proven otherwise, and an entity that carries one component but not the one it needs is unfinished. A component the core does not define passes whatever its name, plain or dotted, its fields unread: this profile knows the core's names alone, and whether another name means anything is a registry's to say, so the name is held to the grammar alone (SPEC §2, ruled 2026-10-18).
$comment: This profile refusing a document does not make the document invalid on the wire. It means the document says something this version of the vocabulary has no definition for — a question for the spec, not a defect in the file.

strict_document.title: the strict overlay
strict_document.description: Where the closure reaches. A component map turns up in four places — on a record, on a template's internals, on a derived node, and inside a tiling's `derives`, which states the components its cells carry — and each is walked here so that the strict reading applies to all of them.
strict_document.$comment: This overlay names the four locations explicitly rather than substituting a schema at the point of use: a `$dynamicRef` would express it in one line, but ajv 8 resolves a cross-resource dynamic anchor to the resource root rather than to the anchored subschema, and a schema layer that only one validator reads correctly is not a schema layer. `derives` is the fourth place, added with v0.6's tiling. If a fifth ever appears, it must be added here — see README.md.

strict_record.description: A record's own components, plus any expansion it carries inline.
strict_record.$comment: Archetype lenses apply only to a record that introduces an entity. A patch, an override or a suppression carries a fragment of one on purpose, and a lens read against a fragment reports a missing component that is sitting in another layer. See README.md, 'What the lenses cannot see'.

strict_derived_map.description: Everything a generator derived, however deep the chain runs. Derived content is machine-written, so it is read strictly but never lensed: an archetype is an authoring aid, and nobody authored this.

whole_entity_components.description: The components of something authored as a whole entity: read strictly, and read through the archetype lenses.

strict_components.description: A component map with every known component closed, plus the reach into a template's internals — which are whole entities in their own right, so they are lensed too — and into a tiling's `derives`, which is a component map like any other.

strict_tiling_derives.description: The components a cell_grid's cells carry, read as strictly as the ones its own record carries. No lens applies: a cell is a fragment of an entity, not a whole one — its pose comes from the tiling.
